title: Sound from who you play: the real switches, one at a time
intro: Headphones help. Stand somewhere with character: next to a wall, cave mouth or building. Start as the Arisen. Press End to start.

steps.text: Taking over your main pawn. Then walk ~15 m away from the Arisen (he follows; that is fine, keep moving).
A (game as it is): sprint until out of breath, swing, jump, walk by the wall. Whose breathing and steps sound close?
B: the pawn you play now has the player's sound settings. Same actions. Different?
B + C1: loudness by distance from the CAMERA. Different?
B + C2: loudness by distance from the PAWN you play. Different from C1?
B + C2 + D: the place's echo and ambience follow the pawn too. Walk in and out of a cave or building if you can.
Back to the Arisen with everything still on (it should all go back to normal on its own). Listen: does the Arisen sound like himself again?
All switches off again. Tell Claude which stage sounded most like playing the pawn yourself, and anything odd (silence, doubled sounds, wrong music).

probes.sound:
local out = {}
local function wc(ch)
  local go = ch and ch:call("get_GameObject")
  return go and go:call("getComponent(System.Type)", sdk.typeof("app.WwiseCharacter")), go and tostring(go:call("get_Name"))
end
local list = {}
pcall(function() list[#list + 1] = sdk.get_managed_singleton("app.CharacterManager"):call("get_ManualPlayer") end)
pcall(function() local l = sdk.get_managed_singleton("app.PawnManager"):call("get_PawnCharacterList"); for i = 0, l:call("get_Count") - 1 do list[#list + 1] = l:call("get_Item", i) end end)
for _, ch in ipairs(list) do
  local w, nm = wc(ch)
  if w then out[#out + 1] = nm .. ":" .. tostring(w:call("get_CharacterCategory")) .. "/" .. string.format("%.2f", w:call("get_CharacterRTPC") or -1) .. "/" .. tostring(w:call("get_IsRTPCTreatedAsPlayer")) end
end
pcall(function() out[#out + 1] = "decayAtPlayer=" .. tostring(sdk.find_type_definition("via.simplewwise.Driver"):get_method("get_CalcDistanceDecayAtPlayerPos"):call(nil)) end)
return table.concat(out, " ")
